articles.summary: 'El Conquistador' apunta a volver a pelear en UFC antes de que acabe al año
articles.body: Dos peleas en UFC y dos victorias para Aleksandre Topuria (7-1)... pero la carrera de 'El Conquistador' está en 'stand-by' desde el pasado 22 de noviembre. Puede ser esa la fecha de su regreso al octágono, pero en este 2026... y de nuevo en Qatar. La información ha salido a escena: el equipo de Santiago Luna (8-1) ha filtrado que la UFC les ha ofrecido la pelea y que se está negociando. MARCA, sin embargo, puede confirmar que el 'staff' de Aleksandre no ha recibido todavía ningún ofrecimiento. Lo que no quita que este combate pueda hacerse para el próximo 21 de noviembre, fecha deslizada por 'MMA Latinoamérica' en redes sociales. Si la oferta llega, aceptarán. Desde el entorno de Aleksandre Topuria lo tienen claro. En caso de ser real el rumor, todo debería precipitarse esta semana o principios de la próxima. Y eso que no es un combate que favorezca demasiado a los intereses del hispanogeorgiano: Luna no está rankeado y viene de perder ante Bryce Mitchell. Es decir, no haría subir demasiado al mayor de los Topuria en caso de victoria. Tiene más que perder... que ganar. Sin embargo, Aleksandre solamente suma dos combates en UFC (dos victorias) en casi dos años desde su debut... y necesita actividad. Mientras Ilia se recupera de sus lesiones (no volverá hasta pasado el mes de febrero de 2027), el mayor de los Topuria debe dar un paso al frente.

articles.title: Jon Jones Train Partner Hints at Possible UFC Return Following Tom Aspinall Injury News
articles.summary: Jon Jones appears to be reconsidering his future in mixed martial arts now that the UFC heavyweight picture has been […]
articles.body:
Jon Jones appears to be reconsidering his future in mixed martial arts now that the UFC heavyweight picture has been thrown into chaos once again.

Earlier this week, Tom Aspinall announced he had vacated the heavyweight title due to his ongoing injuries. The plan had been for Aspinall to rematch Ciryl Gane at UFC 334, but after re-injuring himself in training, the 33-year-old decided he did not want to hold up the division while his return timeline remained unknown.

Aspinall dropping the title drew a reaction from Jones, who questioned the legitimacy of the injury. The two never actually fought, despite Aspinall serving as interim heavyweight champion during Jones' reign atop the division. Jones avoided the matchup at every opportunity and reportedly turned down a $30 million offer from the UFC to make it happen, a stretch that ultimately led to his first retirement from the sport in June 2025 and Aspinall's promotion to undisputed champion.

Jones briefly walked that retirement back and re-entered the UFC's testing pool, but officially retired for good this past April. According to training partner Gable Steveson, Aspinall's title vacation has reignited his interest in competing again.

"I think Ciryl Gane deserves (the undisputed title) he's a fantastic fighter and he's a guy that goes out there and he's beating everybody besides the infinity stones of fighting, (Francis) Ngannou and Jon," Steveson told RMC Sport Combat when asked about the state of the heavyweight division.

"I think Jon would like to come back also, maybe seeing this belt open up put another fire into him. Jon's my training partner everyday in Albuquerque so I've seen what he can still do and I know he can do it at the highest level, and maybe his time will come again and I think it will," Steveson added.

Despite Steveson's comments suggesting Jones is eyeing a comeback, it remains unclear whether UFC CEO Dana White would entertain that possibility at this stage.

With Aspinall stepping away from the title, Gane will be elevated to undisputed champion, since he already holds the interim belt. Gane has received multiple callouts for his first defense, with Josh Hokit requesting a title shot and recent rival Alex Pereira doing the same.

There is speculation that Pereira is the frontrunner to land the fight with Gane, continuing a rematch campaign he has pushed for over the past several months.

Opinion: Jones Returning Would Be A Mistake Worth Making Anyway

Jones sitting out the Aspinall era was always going to invite second-guessing, and Aspinall vacating the belt gives him the cleanest opening yet to walk back his retirement without directly confronting the man he spent years avoiding. That distinction matters more than it might seem. Jones can frame a return as chasing an open title rather than finally answering Aspinall's callouts, which is exactly the kind of narrative control he has built his late career around.

Whether White actually wants this is a separate question, and a fair one. Jones' history of pulling out of fights, combined with a heavyweight division that finally has real momentum behind Gane and Pereira, makes it reasonable for the promotion to move on without him. But UFC has rarely turned down a Jones headline when one was available, and a heavyweight picture this unsettled is exactly the kind of moment that tends to pull him back in.

If Jones does return, expect the promotion to build it around the vacant title rather than a direct Aspinall fight, at least initially. That keeps the door open for the matchup everyone still wants to see, without forcing either side into a fight neither seemed eager to have when it actually mattered.

articles.title: Gable Steveson reacts to Tom Aspinall relinquishing UFC title
articles.summary: Gable Steveson sees Tom Aspinall's title resignation as an opportunity.
articles.body:
In light of Tom Aspinall vacating his UFC title, Gable Steveson has a mixed reaction to the news.

After almost a year away from the octagon, Aspinall has finally relinquished his UFC gold. The Brit is still suffering from the aftermath of an illegal eye poke that ended his UFC 321 title defense prematurely; undergoing several successful surgeries. Now with no undisputed champion in place, the division can move forward. Vocal in their pursuit of a title opportunity, some heavyweights have spoken out on social media about the possibility of fighting for the abandoned throne.

Josh Hokit has been the loudest , claiming that he deserves a shot and has called out interim champion Ciryl Gane to accompany him in the cage. While many believe Hokit deserves his shot, one man who is confident he'll find himself in the title picture soon is Gable Steveson .

But instead of kicking Tom Aspinall while he's down, Steveson offered some words of encouragement for the former titleholder.

"I feel for Tom," Steveson said. "I hope the recovery is going well, and as he posted, it seems like it's really not. So, prayers to him and his family, and make sure he can get back on his feet in the best way possible."

Steveson also knows Tom Aspinall's absence leaves a gaping hole in the weight class. The Olympian is ready to capitalize on the void, believing he is one step closer to UFC gold due to Aspinall's injury.

"I think this is a great opportunity for a lot of young guys like myself, and a few others that are in the heavyweight division to kind of sneak our way in and work hard and get to where we need to go, and in a faster transition," Steveson added.

"So, sorry to him for these complications, but I feel like it's a good thing for us."

articles.title: Ilia Topuria vuelve con todo: "La próxima vez me aseguraré de que revisen los guantes de Justin para que no les ponga nada raro"
articles.standfirst: El 'Matador' lanzó un mensaje en su cuenta de Twitter
articles.summary: El 'Matador' lanzó un mensaje en su cuenta de Twitter
articles.body: Y en su primer tuit tres meses después, Ilia Topuria (17-1) volvió con todo. El 'Matador', que está en Miami completando su recuperación y empezando poco a poco su vuelta a los entrenamientos, lanzó un mensaje en sus redes sociales avisando de su retorno... y con un dardo a Justin Gaethje (28-5), el nuevo campeón del peso ligero tras coronarse en UFC Casa Blanca. Este fue el mensaje de Ilia Topuria: "Últimas pruebas médicas hechas. He vuelto. A todos los payasos que han estado hablando mal de mí y dándome por perdido todo este tiempo, aquí estoy. Ahora veamos quién tiene pelotas. Gracias a todos por el apoyo. La próxima vez me aseguraré de que revisen los guantes de Justin para que no les ponga nada raro. Nos vemos pronto". El peleador ahora afincado en Miami entró de lleno en la polémica que hubo post-combate sobre los guantes de Gaethje. Muchos aficionados insinuaron (sin pruebas) que el estadounidense había alterado sus guantes introduciendo algo en su anterior para que los golpes impactaran con mayor fuerza en el cuerpo y rostro del 'Matador'. Un asunto que se había disipado con el paso de los meses... pero que ahora está de vuelta por el tuit de Topuria. Durante toda su carrera, el doble campeón hispanogeorgiano había habituado a sus fans a ser un usuario activo en Twitter. Y ahora, ya recuperado de sus lesiones en UFC Casa Blanca, Topuria está de vuelta en todos los aspectos. Ilia caldea el ambiente de cara a una posible revancha con Gaethje, que es lo que tanto él como su equipo buscan: recuperar el título del peso ligero lo más pronto posible y demostrar que el pasado 14 de junio únicamente fue una mala noche.

articles.title: Ilia Topuria ‘back’ after clearing medical tests, blames Justin Gaethje’s ‘weird’ gloves for UFC White House loss
articles.summary: Ilia Topuria is officially back — and apparently armed with one of the wildest excuses imaginable. The former two-division Ultimate Fighting Championship (UF...
articles.body:
Ilia Topuria is officially back — and apparently armed with one of the wildest excuses imaginable.

The former two-division Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) champion announced today (Weds., Sept. 16, 2026) that he has completed his final medical tests and is cleared to resume his career following the horrific beating he suffered against Justin Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 in June 2026.

However, buried inside Topuria's fiery return announcement was an absolutely insane suggestion that Gaethje may have loaded or otherwise tampered with his gloves before handing "El Matador" the first loss of his professional career.

"Final medical tests done. I'm back," Topuria wrote on Twitter. "To all the clowns who've been talking shit and counting me out this whole time, here I am. Now let's see who's got the balls. Thanks to everyone for the support. Next time I'll make sure they check Justin's gloves so he doesn't put anything weird on them. See you soon."

"By the way Justin, f—k you. And Ali, f—k you too."

Yes, Topuria genuinely appears to be buying into the ridiculous conspiracy theory pushed by a small portion of his fanbase following UFC White House.

The theory claimed Gaethje had something illegal inside his gloves — or "bricks," as "The Highlight" jokingly described it — because of the extraordinary damage he inflicted upon Topuria. Gaethje and longtime head coach Trevor Wittman already laughed off the baseless accusations during an appearance on The Joe Rogan Experience .

"What a compliment," Gaethje said. "People saying I'm juiced, what a compliment. People saying I've got bricks in my f—king gloves, what a compliment."

There has been zero credible evidence that Gaethje tampered with his gloves, loaded his hand wraps or did anything illegal before the fight. No commission official or UFC representative has raised concerns about Gaethje's equipment.

Gaethje simply beat the hell out of Topuria.

After surviving a dangerous second round, Gaethje took control and battered the previously undefeated champion until Topuria's corner stopped the fight before the fifth round. Topuria suffered two broken orbital bones and severe facial damage and was immediately transported to a local hospital .

The glove accusation is also a dramatic departure from Topuria's original reaction. In his first statement after the loss, Topuria insisted there were "no excuses," acknowledged Gaethje's performance , and admitted his rival had delivered on his promise to leave a mark on his face.

Three months later, the excuses have arrived.

Topuria did not reveal when he plans to compete again or whether UFC will grant him an immediate rematch. UFC CEO Dana White recently confirmed that Topuria is ready to return and expressed interest in either a second Gaethje fight or the long-awaited grudge match against Paddy Pimblett .

Whenever Topuria returns, he may want to focus on correcting the tactical mistakes that cost him the title instead of checking Gaethje's gloves for imaginary foreign objects.

articles.title: Chael Sonnen apologizes to Tom Aspinall over injury drama: 'We got this wrong'
articles.summary: "I feel terrible for the guy," the UFC Hall of Famer said of Aspinall. "If there's any injury I could have, the last one I would want is something with my ey...
articles.body:
It already seemed as if it couldn't get any worse for Tom Aspinall and his pursuit of an active UFC heavyweight championship reign. Then, complications from his lingering eye injuries led him to vacate the title .

Aspinall announced Monday on social media that he was giving up the title he originally won as an interim championship in November 2023. That same title later became undisputed when Jon Jones retired and relinquished his belt in June 2025. In Aspinall's first defense of the undisputed title in October 2025, he infamously fought to a first-round no-contest against Ciryl Gane after suffering multiple grisly eye-pokes .

Given how common eye-pokes have been throughout UFC history, the length of Aspinall's injury woes sparked widespread speculation on their legitimacy. Even pundits and UFC Hall of Famers like Chael Sonnen questioned what was going on with Aspinall.

After the saga reached the point of Aspinall giving up the title, Sonnen apologized to the now-former champion on Tuesday's edition of "The Ariel Helwani Show."

"I'm so sorry for what Tom Aspinall went through, and I even look back at some of my words and opinions that were clearly wrong. There is clearly a medical issue here," Sonnen told Uncrowned.

"We got this wrong. Guys get poked in the eye all the time, and they keep on fighting. Then, when the stakes were this big, we didn't know. We got it wrong, and I feel terrible for the guy. If there's any injury I could have, the last one I would want is something with my eyes.

"That's a very real life thing that can impact you. You've got to be very careful."

In Aspinall's absence, the man who infamously fouled him, Gane, claimed a newly-created interim title by defeating Alex Pereira at UFC Freedom 250 on the White House's South Lawn in June. The UFC has yet to make a public statement on whether or not Aspinall's decision automatically makes Gane the new undisputed heavyweight champion.

Regardless of how the divisional landscape shakes out, Sonnen expects Aspinall won't lose his seat atop the division once he's ready to return. Sonnen compared the situation to those of past champions like Georges St-Pierre, who gave up their titles mid-reign or at the peak of their powers.

"Tom's going to be back, and when he is, he's going to be in that exact same spot, right?" Sonnen said. "He's going to be fighting in a main event for the undisputed heavyweight championship of the world. Things in his life are not going to change, so this is just purely a 'get-well, Tom.'

"I do think it was handled right. I do think that it was handled with grace, and I think that aside from the UFC doing it right, I think Tom did a tremendous job."

That brings us to what's next for the division.

Sonnen believes Gane's championship promotion is imminent. And waiting in the wings appears to be either a rematch with Pereira or a defense against surging contender Josh Hokit . However, the bad blood that's continued to fester between Hokit and Pereira since UFC Freedom 250 — Hokit defeated Derrick Lewis on the same White House card — has opened the door for that fight, said Sonnen, as well as fellow contender Alexander Volkov.

"[UFC is] goin g to elevate Ciryl. They've already got something in place for what they're going to do. The question becomes, who's going to fight Ciryl?" Sonnen said.

"I have a fear that Josh Hokit, who is trying to get the nod against Ciryl over the proverbial battle that he is having with Alex Pereira right now — I fear that Josh, on accident, by way of dismissing Alex, is inadvertently creating a massive fight against Alex. And you're going to have to bring Volkov in at some point, you're going to have to take the risk and do that match."

A fight between Gane and Volkov would be their third, with Gane holding a 2-0 lead in the series. The pair's rematch in December 2024, however, was a highly controversial split decision, which many argued should have gone in favor of the towering Russian. Gane won the first fight via a five-round unanimous decision in June 2021.

In total, Volkov has won six of his past seven bouts since 2022, except for that close Gane rematch.

In his perfect world, Sonnen would give Hokit the next crack at Gane, but he sees Volkov as a factor that could become hard to ignore in the conversation.

"You're going to have to pay an integrity to the rankings at some point," Sonnen said. "They're not going to be able to have Volkov win another fight, whoever that's against, and then not give him the chance. So Volkov is right there. Not to mention he was very competitive with Ciryl. I believe he beat Ciryl and lost the decision, so does Dana White and Hunter Campbell. So, at some point, there is a human element, not to mention he's got the ranking.

"Imagine a card where you're going to do Volkov and Ciryl, and a lot of people for the press conference go, 'Ah.' But on that same card, you put Hokit and Pereira. Now, all of a sudden, much like Arman Tsarukyan and [Mauricio] Ruffy came in to really help and support their own main event [at UFC 331], I think all of a sudden that makes a little bit of sense. Because if you don't do that, then you're going to have to do Volkov versus some form of a title shot one fight from now, and you might not have the coverage of Hokit-Pereira."

articles.title: Ilia Topuria Accuses Justin Gaethje of Cheating at UFC White House Fight, Provides Injury Update
articles.summary: After his loss to Justin Gaethje at UFC's Freedom 250 in June, Ilia Topuria accused the lightweight champion of glove manipulation.
articles.body:
After his loss to Justin Gaethje at UFC's Freedom 250 in June, Ilia Topuria accused the lightweight champion of glove manipulation.

In a post updating his injury status, Topuria said the next time he fights Gaethje, he'll "check Justin's gloves so he doesn't put anything weird on them."

"Final medical tests done. I'm back. To all the clowns who've been talking s--t and counting me out this whole time, here I am," he wrote on social media. "Now let's see who's got the balls. Thanks to everyone for the support. Next time I'll make sure they check Justin's gloves so he doesn't put anything weird on them. See you soon."

Topuria had an undefeated record coming into the fight and was looking to defend his lightweight title for a third time in the fight. Gaethje was competing for the lightweight title for the first time since 2022.

Topuria sustained significant facial damage in the bout, with the fight nearly being stopped before the start of the fourth round. His corner eventually ended the fight before the final round.

As a result of the facial damage, Topuria broke both orbital bones but did not need surgery.

It was by far the most damage Topuria has taken during his career, and it's easy to see why he was quick to accuse Gaethje of cheating. Whether anything will come out of the investigation remains to be seen.

But one thing that is clear is that a rematch between Topuria and Gaethje could be on the way, especially after the bold claim from Topuria on Wednesday.

articles.title: Tito Ortiz wants to end decades of bad blood with Dana White: 'I've tried to apologize'
articles.summary: "If that bridge could ever be hashed back together between me and Dana, I would love it," said the UFC legend. "But I know Dana. He's not that type of guy."
articles.body:
Tito Ortiz was never afraid to make enemies throughout his legendary MMA career. But in hindsight, the UFC Hall of Famer wishes he could take back one of his greatest rivalries.

As one of the first true superstars amid UFC's early rise, Ortiz lived up to his "Huntington Beach Bad Boy" nickname for reasons that extended beyond the Octagon. His attitude didn't always align with those around him, most notably including UFC CEO Dana White.

White and Ortiz publicly butted heads throughout the latter's entire run with the company from 1997 to 2012. On Wednesday's edition of "The Ariel Helwani Show," the former UFC light heavyweight champion admitted he regrets how he handled his experience with White, and noted he's even tried to reconcile in recent years.

"I've tried to reach out a few times. I've tried to do interviews and apologize, just saying that I'm sorry for what I did. I was a young kid," Ortiz told Uncrowned.

"I said some things about him a few times that I probably shouldn't have. I shouldn't have went over and above, but I didn't understand. Negotiation tactics that I learned, I learned from him — I tried to use his own negotiation tactics on himself, which I shouldn't have done that. I was influenced by others that I shouldn't have been influenced by. I should have thought what I thought and what was right. I made some bad decisions, and I've tried to apologize for that."

One moment in particular stood out for Ortiz when he thought about his greatest regrets in dealing with White. At UFC 84 in May 2008, Ortiz fought Lyoto Machida and infamously showed up at the weigh-ins wearing a T-shirt that read, "Dana is my b****."

"Wearing the T-shirt I did before the Machida fight, I probably shouldn't have did that," Ortiz said. "A few interviews that I said some things, I probably shouldn't have done. But at the time, like I said, I was just trying to fight for my future as a fighter. I know I'm not going to be able to compete for the rest of my life. I knew this company was going to be as big as it is now. So, I was just trying to get paid a little bit more money.

"That was one of the big things that Dana always said: 'Don't talk about money to the public.' But to me, I wanted to take care of my family forever."

Having been one of the UFC's biggest stars of the promotion's early years, Ortiz, 51, is now comfortably phased out of fight life, having not competed in MMA since 2019. Ortiz now runs his own restaurant in Florida, Tito's Cantina , and makes a living there.

He wonders if things would've been different if his relationship with White was better.

"I'm a blue-collar guy now. I still gotta get up, and I gotta work," Ortiz said. "I have a little bit of an advantage by being Tito Ortiz, and I have some amazing fans that respect me and still come to my restaurant. I still do public appearances. I still do public speaking. I do these other things because I made my name as Tito Ortiz, because the UFC has given me that opportunity.

"At the end of the day, I shouldn't have to do these things. I shouldn't have to worry about my bills being paid, because I've fought my a** for 16 years for the UFC and helped them get on the track of where they are right now.

"I'm thankful for the track they gave me and the opportunities they gave me through my career, but it's a double-edged sword. I messed up," Ortiz continued. "It is part of the deal. If that bridge could ever be hashed back together between me and Dana, I would love it. But I know Dana. He's not that type of guy. I know what type of guy he is, and he's not that type of guy.

"It's hurtful, but it's OK. I'm thankful for my fans. My fans have never forgotten about who I am, and I'm thankful for it."

Ortiz's induction into the UFC Hall of Fame in 2012 is arguably the closest thing to reconciliation he's had with White and the promotion since his departure more than a decade ago. Yet, Ortiz still isn't in good enough graces to be treated like anything more than a fan.

When the UFC was in Miami for UFC 327 in April, Ortiz said he was denied a single ticket upon his inquiry. He admitted that the lack of appreciation the promotion has shown for his era of UFC legends bothers him.

"I asked just for one ticket, and they said no. So I ended up buying a ticket. It cost me $1,000. Dana just doesn't like me," Ortiz said.

"I'm not going to sit here and beg. I'm not begging for anything. That's the way he feels, OK. It is what it is. He's gambling millions and millions every night, but take care of the guys that got you here.

"Once again, I don't want anything from him. I laid my own bed. I made it. I'm OK with it. It is what it is. But like former football players, basketball players, they're sitting front row. I think they deserve it. MMA fighters, same thing. Randy Couture, myself, [Quinton] 'Rampage' [Jackson], so many other fighters that have spoken up and have pretty much been erased from UFC. That's one thing they can't do, though, because of the fans — the fans will never forget us."

articles.title: Arman Tsarukyan, NHL player? UFC 331 star describes what could've been
articles.summary: Before it was the UFC, Arman Tsarukyan set sights on the NHL.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES – Before he was a UFC superstar and world-famous streamer, Arman Tsarukyan had dreams of being known for his abilities on ice.

Tsarukyan (23-3 MMA, 10-2 UFC) co-headlines Saturday's UFC 331 at Crypto.com Arena ( Paramount+ ) and what a journey it's been. His athletic origins haven't always been fight-centric, Tsarukyan revealed Wednesday. Apparently, hockey was his first love and is still something he's passionate about.

"I wanted to be a hockey player," Tsarukyan told MMA Junkie and other reporters at a pre-fight news conference Wednesday. "My dream was to go to the U.S. and play in the NHL. But I couldn't be a good hockey player, and then I started working. I didn't like working, and I became a fighter. Because of fighting, now I'm in U.S. and fighting in the best promotion in UFC. My hockey career was so good. I love hockey and when I have time even now sometimes I play."

Born in Armenia, Tsarukyan doesn't associate with a specific NHL team. However, his favorite player he revealed without hesitation.

"I like (Alexander) Ovechkin ," Tsarukyan said.

How far Tsarukyan would've gone in hockey remains unclear, but it's almost certainly not as far as he's gone in the fight world. A win Saturday over Mauricio Ruffy could get him the long-awaited title shot he's dreamed of.

"Yeah, 100 percent," Tsarukyan said of what his odds are of fighting for gold should he win Saturday.

Despite radiating confidence, Tsarukyan didn't hold back on his compliments of Ruffy (14-2 MMA, 5-1 UFC), the tricky and flashy striker who trains alongside former UFC middleweight champion Israel Adesanya and current UFC featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski . While Tsarukayn admitted Ruffy is a unique test unlike any he's faced before, his prediction didn't waver. The biggest thing he thinks he needs to do is weather the storm, and the fight will be his.

"You cannot compare Adesanya with me," Tsarukyan said. "You cannot compare Volkanovski with me. It's completely different fighters. He has the power and he has good striking, but I'm better everywhere with my wrestling and my striking that I can mix. I can over-strike him."

articles.summary: Jon Jones hasn't fought since November 2024, when he successfully defended his heavyweight title, and Gable Steveson believes he could come back to claim the title once again.
articles.body:
Jon Jones hasn't fought since November 2024, when he successfully defended his heavyweight title, and Gable Steveson believes he could come back to claim the title once again.

Steveson teased a possible title fight for Jones if he chooses to return to the UFC.

"I called Jon today, and he's honored to have the opportunity to maybe come back," Steveson said. "He's always had gold around his waist."

Jones beat Stipe Miocic at UFC 309 to defend his heavyweight title for the first time, and he shortly after expressed interest in a heavyweight title unification bout with Tom Aspinall.

Jones has since retired, but there have been several indications that he's not done fighting.

He reentered the UFC's drug-testing pool last July, shortly after the UFC 250 event at the White House was announced, though he ended up not being on the card for that event.

Now could be the perfect time for him to officially make his return.

Aspinall vacated the UFC heavyweight title due to "ongoing complications" with his eye, meaning Ciryl Gane was promoted to the undisputed champion. Jones may have wanted to fight Aspinall initially, but he might instead have the chance to take back the title against Gane.

articles.title: Amy Broadhurst continues comeback at European championships: 'This will be my last shot at the Olympics'
articles.summary: Amy Broadhurst is continuing her boxing comeback after becoming a mother; A World and European gold medallist for Ireland, Broadhurst has switched to GB and will box for Britain at the European Championships, her first major tournament since having a baby
articles.body:
Amy Broadhurst, a former World and European gold medallist for Ireland, will be part of the squad boxing for Britain.

Broadhurst, a key sparring partner for Katie Taylor for the Irish legend's first iconic victory over Amanda Serrano, switched from Ireland to Britain ahead of Paris 2024 as she sought to qualify for the Olympic Games.

These European championships will be her first major championships since returning to competition after the birth of her baby boy.

"It's tough but we're making it work and I'm very lucky to have the support around me," Broadhurst told Sky Sports . "He's at the right age now where this is possible.

"He'll come to Bulgaria with me and he comes to Sheffield every second week with me," she continued. "Those weeks are tough because you're doing two jobs then.

"This is my last shot at the Olympics. So they know after this it's all said and done."

These Europeans will be a key step on a journey that she hopes will eventually take her to LA 2028. But her return to boxing has already been eventful. The first bout in her comeback earlier this year saw her drawn against her old team.

"My first fight back after two years was against Ireland. So that was a mad situation," she said.

"I was trying to control my feelings because obviously a lot of [stuff] went on with that whole situation.

"I knew going in that I was going to do okay. But there was just a lot of ill feelings on both behalfs. I think I handled it very well. I shook hands with the coach and I showed respect. That was probably the main thing, not to get sucked into the emotional part of it. It was get in, box and move on. It was like closing the chapter on something. We shook hands and then that's it."

She didn't box Ireland's top lightweight then but that could potentially happen in Sofia. Kellie Harrington, Ireland's two-time Olympic champion, has entered these Europeans.

"I was her sparring partner for the 2021 Games," Broadhurst said. "I was brought over to Tokyo.

"We've shared the ring many times and it would be a spicy fight.

"You could meet each other," Broadhurst noted. "You just don't know what's going to happen.

articles.title: MMA: Irish fighter Adam Darby reflects on journey to UFC after earning Dana White Contender Series contract
articles.summary: Dublin mixed martial artist Adam Darby says more than a decade of hard work came "to fruition" after becoming the first Irish fighter to earn a UFC contract through Dana White's Contender Series.
articles.body:
Mixed martial artist Adam Darby says more than a decade of hard work came "to fruition" after becoming the first Irish fighter to earn a UFC contract through Dana White's Contender Series.

Darby (8-1) secured his place on the UFC roster with an impressive TKO victory over American Patrick Rivera (13-5) in Las Vegas on 1 September.

The welterweight dominated Rivera before the bout ended in the third round via doctor stoppage.

Darby was one of five fighters awarded UFC contracts on the night, completing an arduous journey which included a 20-second defeat by Mush Aslani and a 17-month absence because of a serious hand injury.

"I was just sitting there thinking to myself, well, that's 10-plus years of work all coming to fruition," Darby told BBC Sport NI.

The Dubliner had controlled the contest against Rivera but was hoping the fight would continue long enough for him to secure a more emphatic finish.

"I was saying to the referee, 'Don't stop it, he's good, he's good,'" he said.

"I knew he was done, but I wanted a highlight-reel finish. The ref recognised the damage he was taking and pulled the plug on it.

"I went in there to put on a show, and I think I delivered."

Liverpool's Liam McCracken also competed on the card but missed out on a UFC contract after suffering a knockout defeat by Silvestre Sanchez in a thrilling lightweight contest.

The former Cage Warriors fighter's journey started when his father enrolled him in kickboxing, but upon discovering MMA, he was hooked.

"Once I had my first day in MMA, that was it," he said.

"That was me for the rest of my life, and now here we are over 10 years later and I'm a professional UFC fighter."

That conviction was evident in a note Darby wrote in 2018 and shared on social media following his Contender Series victory.

It read: "One life, one chance, UFC or nothing."

"Visualisation is very important, but you can't sit in your bedroom looking in the mirror saying, 'I'm the best of the best,' and not training and backing it up," he said.

"You have to set some goals and put the work in to get to where you want to be. I had to put the work in."

But the Clongriffin fighter, who is currently on a seven-fight winning streak, encountered several setbacks in pursuit of his UFC dream.

He entered his second professional fight believing he was 'the best guy in the world', only to suffer a standing TKO defeat by Aslani.

"For a lot of people that might finish their career," he said.

"But for me, that loss made me reflect, 'where am I going to go from here?'

"You can't let something like that set you back. Life's going to hit you hard, but you have to be able to come back from it."

A greater obstacle followed when Darby suffered serious hand and finger injuries before Cage Warriors 170 bout in March 2024, requiring multiple operations and 17 months away from competition.

"I snapped my finger in half, I broke my hand, I had to have multiple surgeries to get it back right," Darby said.

"I was told, 'You probably won't fight again, you won't be able to punch with that.'

"That was two and a half years ago, and here I am now."

Darby hopes his achievement can inspire another generation of Irish fighters to follow him into the UFC.

"It's inspiring to think somebody watching me in five or 10 years' time in the UFC might say, 'I saw Adam Darby do it so I knew I could do it,'" he said.

"The area I come from, not a lot of people make it out like this and do so well.

"So it's good to show people that you can earn an honest living and do fighting and make some money out of it."

The Team Ryano fighter believes the standard of Irish MMA has risen significantly, with more fighters now able to dedicate themselves fully to the sport.

"The standard of MMA in Ireland has improved so much. The fighters before us worked multiple jobs their whole career, now everybody is training full-time," he said.

"Looking at the guys coming through at Cage Warriors, Paddy McCorry, Ger Harris, Solomon Simon, these guys are only 12 to 24 months away from the UFC."

Having spent more than a decade trying to reach the promotion, Darby is now targeting his UFC debut before the end of the year.

"I'll definitely be targeting one more fight this year, but it's up to UFC now," he said.

"I've always told them I'm ready to fight whenever they want me to."

articles.title: Gaethje responde a Topuria: "Lo mejor que se te ocurrió es una excusa lamentable"
articles.standfirst: El peleador estadounidense no ha tardado en salir al paso del ataque de 'El Matador' en redes sociales
articles.summary: El peleador estadounidense no ha tardado en salir al paso del ataque de 'El Matador' en redes sociales
articles.body: Anoche, Ilia Topuria volvió por todo lo alto a la actividad en su cuenta de 'X' con un tuit donde afirmaba que estaba de vuelta y lanzaba un ataque a Justin Gaethje para caldear el ambiente. Ese movimiento tuvo su efecto, ya que al poco tiempo el peleador estadounidense lanzó una respuesta que no hace más que avivar el beef entre ambos y dar motivos a la UFC para realizar una revancha en cuanto ambos estén listos. El pasado 14 de junio Topuria perdió ante Gaethje en el UFC Casa Blanca, por lo que su objetivo número uno en este momento es vengar esa derrota. A pesar de que Justin dijo en un principio que 'El Matador' no se merecía la revancha, su discurso cambió durante las últimas semanas y afirmó que la última palabra la tenía la UFC. Las opciones para Ilia son claras: Gaethje o Paddy Pimblett. Obviamente, Topuria prefiere redimirse de su traspiés ante 'The Highlight', y ha dado un paso de gigante después de atacarle y conseguir su cometido. "94 días y lo mejor que se te ocurrió es una excusa lamentable. Tan terrible como tu última actuación. Hazlo mejor, pequeño", respondió Gaethje a Topuria, que ha dejado caer que la próxima vez revisará las guantillas de Justin para que no ocurra nada raro. El tuit de Ilia se refería a la polémica que hubo en torno a las guantillas del estadounidense y los daños que causaron sus golpes en el rostro del peleador hispanogeorgiano. Salió a la luz una foto donde parecía que Justin tenía algo dentro de la guantilla, y Topuria ha hablado acerca de esa conspiración para que su tuit se llene de interacciones y 'The Highlight' responda. El objetivo está cumplido, ya que apenas pasó media hora cuando Gaethje entró al trapo. Bueno, Gaethje o Ali Abdelaziz -su agente-, que se dice que suele llevar las redes sociales de sus peleadores. Por si las moscas, Topuria puso otro tuit para salir de dudas. "Por cierto, Justin, jódete. Y Ali, jódete tú también". Un regreso por todo lo alto de Ilia, que no se ha guardado nada y quiere que la rivalidad siga creciendo. Su regreso se espera para inicios de 2027, al igual que el de Gaethje, que reconoció hace poco que todavía no podía golpear fuerte porque le dolían las manos. Por tanto, la UFC tiene una oportunidad de oro para realizar una revancha que cada vez gana más enteros y le daría a 'El Matador' la posibilidad de redimirse.

articles.title: Justin Gaethje rejects Ilia Topuria's claim that he cheated to win White House fight
articles.summary: UFC lightweight champion Justin Gaethje tells Ilia Topuria he needs to "do better" after insinuating he cheated to win their fight at UFC Freedom 250 in June.
articles.body:
UFC lightweight champion Justin Gaethje has rejected Ilia Topuria's insinuation that he cheated to win their fight at UFC Freedom 250 in June.

Topuria, 29, retired on his stool at the end of the fourth round, losing the title on the South Lawn of the White House in Washington DC.

The Georgian-Spaniard was previously unbeaten but sustained serious injuries to his eye in the defeat as American Gaethje became undisputed champion for the first time.

After a three-month recovery period, Topuria confirmed on X that he has recovered and is ready to return to the octagon, while also taking aim at Gaethje.

"Final medical tests done. I'm back," Topuria posted.

"To all the clowns who've been counting me out this whole time, here I am.

"Next time I'll make sure they check Justin's gloves so he doesn't put anything weird on them. See you soon."

Responding to those allegations, Gaethje, 37, replied: "94 days and the best you could come up with is a lame excuse. As terrible as your last performance. Do better kid."

Topuria reigned as featherweight champion before vacating the title and moving up a division to beat Charles Oliveira for the vacant lightweight belt.

He was making his first defence against interim champion Gaethje.

Gaethje is yet to book his next fight and a rematch between the pair could be on the cards, although Arman Tsarukyan, who faces Mauricio Ruffy, at UFC 331 on Saturday claims UFC president Dana White has promised a title shot to the winner.

Hasta ahora no nos dejaban asistir porque una normativa lo impedía. Pero las MMA no son violencia. Las MMA son deporte, son disciplina, son respeto y son esfuerzo", empezaba Izán. "Porque yo aquí desde el Levium Armorum, el gimnasio de Fabià Sintes, me han ayudado a explicar por qué nuestro deporte nos ayuda tanto a los niños. Y era muy injusto que no pudiéramos ver en directo a nuestros referentes. Pero más injusto era que no pudiéramos disfrutar esta pasión junto a nuestras familias. Pero hoy ya podemos hacerlo. Así que sí, hoy estoy muy feliz. Porque esto no es sólo que nos dejen entrar a un evento, esto es sentir que por fin se nos ha escuchado y que se ha entendido que las MMA también son un deporte. Y para mí eso significa muchísimo. Así que sólo queda disfrutar de algo que hasta ahora no podía hacer", finalizaba.

articles.title: B/R Staff Predictions for UFC 331 Main Card
articles.summary: UFC 331 goes down this Saturday in Los Angeles, and the early signs point to a very exciting night of fights.
articles.body:
UFC 331 goes down this Saturday in Los Angeles, and the early signs point to a very exciting night of fights.

The card will be headlined by a flyweight title fight, with champion Joshua Van taking on returning former champ, Alexandre Pantoja. It will be the second time the pair meet in the Octagon, though their first encounter can barely be called a fight, as Pantoja suffered a fluke arm injury less than 30 seconds in, resulting in a TKO loss and the crowning of a new champ. Their rematch will hopefully provide a much more decisive outcome.

The UFC 331 co-main event is also a huge fight, as Arman Tsarukyan takes on Mauricio Ruffy at lightweight. Both men are among the top contenders in their division, but Tsarukyan in particular might just lock up a title shot if he wins impressively.

Before we get to that, we'll get a fan-friendly featherweight fight between former Bellator champ Patricio "Pitbull" Freire and "The Korean Superboy" Doo Ho Choi. The main card will kick off with a heavyweight fight between super prospect Gable Steveson and huge underdog Sean Sharaf, and a light heavyweight clash pitting veteran contender Alonzo Menifield against unbeaten prospect Iwo Baraniewski.

As always, the B/R combat sports squad has you covered for pre-fight predictions. Here's how we see it all going down in LA.

Lyle Fitzsimmons: I thought Pantoja would win the first one. I believe he'll win this one. I know Van has won seven straight, including the "win" over Pantoja and a subsequent defense over Tatsuro Taira. But let's not forget Pantoja was on an eight-fight heater before losing his belt.

Pantoja has fought better guys and beaten better guys. I thought he was operating at a higher level in December, and I still believe it.

Prediction: Pantoja by unanimous decision

Adam Kramer: The first time these two fought, we were given only 26 seconds of action.

An elbow injury ended Alexandre Pantoja's night, giving Joshua Van the title belt under deeply unfortunate circumstances. It was weird, and we were deprived of a tremendous fight.

Seeing Pantoja as an underdog in the rematch is still frankly jarring. The fact that Van was able to largely handle Tatsuro Taira during his fight in May is likely a good reason.

Beyond his remarkable takedown defense, Van showcased incredible cardio. That will serve him well once again against Pantoja, who has gone the distance in multiple five-round wars over the past few years.

Van's ability to stay on his feet will be crucial, although Pantoja presents a much different style than Taira. He is better equipped to turn his punches and movements into takedowns, and in turn, he will likely try everything in his power to turn those awkward exchanges into potential submissions.

I love what we've seen from Van thus far, although this feels like a different challenge. Pantoja finds an opening and takes full advantage.

Prediction: Pantoja by submission, Rd. 3

Tom Taylor: Looks like I'll be playing devil's advocate on this one.

I like Pantoja and am happy to call him the second-best flyweight in UFC history behind the great Demetrious "Mighty Mouse" Johnson. However, I've been on the Van hype train since he first arrived in the UFC, and after his thrilling beatdown of Tatsuro Taira, I'm pretty confident he's reached a new level as a champion.

Van will need to be very careful against Pantoja, particularly when they inevitably hit the mat, but I think his cardio, striking and firepower should carry him to victory over five rounds—assuming Pantoja's legendary durability holds up at 36 years old.

Lyle Fitzsimmons: Another five-rounder in the co-main between two red-hot fighters, and another case—at least to Fitz's oldish eyes—of one guy having simply succeeded on a higher level.

Tsarukyan hasn't lost since 2022. The guys he's handled since then, including Beneil Dariush, Charles Oliveira, and Dan Hooker, are simply better than anything Ruffy's beaten.

Prediction: Tsarukyan by unanimous decision

Adam Kramer: Let's start with the obvious. There is enormous pressure on Arman Tsarukyan in this fight.

Given that he's fought twice since the start of 2024—working his way into Dana White's doghouse along the way—a loss here could certainly hinder the fresh momentum he's trying to build.

His opponent is not a slouch, either. While Mauricio Ruffy was not initially Tsarukyan's opponent, he's still plenty dangerous. He's won four of his past five fights—the one loss came via Benoit Saint-Denis's submission.

That result feels noteworthy for this fight given the style Tsarukyan is likely to bring. He doesn't have to win by submission, which he did against Dan Hooker last time out. But his wrestling, grappling, and potential submission skills are likely to come into play, and a five-round fight suits his style extraordinarily well.

Ruffy, of course, is certainly dangerous on his feet. But can he stay there? And for how long?

Tsarukyan proves he's one of the sport's dangerous fighters once again.

Prediction: Tsarukyan by Submission, Rd. 2

Tom Taylor: I'm going to be honest. I'm not really sold on Arman Tsarukyan. He's definitely very good, but it's hard for me to forget his decision loss to Mateusz Gamrot, which has aged quite poorly. I also don't trust the guy to show up in top form—or even show up at all—when he seems to spend all his time running around with streamers and influencers.

But I digress. As Adam stated, Tsarukyan seems to have the perfect style to deal with Ruffy. He is an elite grappler—at least as good as Ruffy's recent foil, Benoit Saint-Denis—and should be able to take him down and finish him. Ruffy's recent training with Alexander Volkanovski gives me some confidence that he might be able to pull this one out, and I would definitely love to see it happen. However, the obvious pick is still Tsarukyan inside the distance.

Prediction: Tsarukyan by submission, Rd. 3

Lyle Fitzsimmons: Hey, didn't you use to be Patricio Pitbull?

That's got to be the vibe around the 39-year-old Brazilian after three decidedly non-transcendent fights—a win and two losses—in the UFC since he ended his long belt-toting run in the Bellator promotion.

He's gone from facing a former title challenger, Yair Rodriguez, in his octagonal debut to a 35-year-old mid-carder, Doo Ho Choi, who's coming off a win over Daniel Santos and is barely three years clear of a draw with Kyle Nelson.

Prediction: Pitbull by unanimous decision

Adam Kramer: The reality for Patricio Pitbull is pretty simple. He's lost three of his last five fights and has finished only one opponent during that time. He is, of course, a legend regardless of what happens here, but his performances of late, at 39-years-old, don't exactly ooze excellence.

The issue with this particular opponent starts with size and reach. Doo Ho Choi is four inches taller than Pitbull and has a massive reach advantage. Beyond that, he is a more active, dangerous fighter.

Pitbull would be wise to grapple here, though his opponent's danger could prompt another conservative effort.

In this instance, Choi's volume prevails yet again.

Tom Taylor: I'm leaning Choi on this one, largely for the reasons Adam mentioned. The Korean is rangy, powerful, and always has his foot on the gas, which I see causing some serious problems for the unsung legend known as "Pitbull."

Pitbull is apparently still quite durable, having recently survived some heavy fire from Aaron Pico, but I was watching live when he was knocked out by Chihiro Suzuki in the Rizin ring in 2023, so I'm not confident he'll survive three rounds either.

Still, I'll give him the benefit of the doubt.

Lyle Fitzsimmons: I was ready and willing to say Menifield was rugged enough and savvy enough to take on a guy on a run of nine straight first-round KOs. But then I remembered Menifield was dusted in 87 seconds by Volkan Oezdemir just 10 months ago, so consider my mind changed.

Adam Kramer: If this fight goes the distance, I will fight Alex Pereira.

In other words, make sure you're not late for this one, because the likelihood of a knockout seems incredibly high.

Alonzo Menifield has the experience, and perhaps that will be the deciding factor. It would behoove him to grapple and close the distance. And pushing Iwo Baraniewski to a second round, something that hasn't happened since 2004, would also be ideal.

The problem? Menifield's chin hasn't been superb of late, and this feels like a legitimate prospect coming into his own. It wouldn't shock me if Baraniewski ended this within two minutes.

Tom Taylor: Looks like we're unanimous on this one.

Menifield is definitely the toughest test of Baraniewski's career so far, but this still looks like it's going to be one-way traffic. Baraniewski has won his last seven fights by first-round stoppage, and Menifield has been knocked out four times since joining the UFC—including a loss to Volkan Oezdemir less than a year ago, as Lyle said.

All of that makes this is a pretty easy call.

Welcome to the light heavyweight top-15, Mr. Baraniewski.

Lyle Fitzsimmons: Ever wondered what it felt like to be on a list to be fed to the lions?

The 33-year-old has been stopped in the second round in two straight fights, and he gets promoted to Saturday's main card to face the rampaging Gable Steveson, who's won each of four pro fights—including two in the UFC—in less than four minutes.

Adam Kramer: The biggest favorite on the card by a wide margin, Gable Steveson has a chance to once again showcase his evolving skill set against an opponent that, if we're being completely honest, feels wildly outclassed.

Will he wrestle? Will he throw those massive knees we saw in his previous fight against Elisha Ellison? We shall see.

Chances are, he'll probably save the wrestling for when he truly needs it, and this doesn't feel like that moment. Instead, I think we will see him try to put on a show. Don't blink, because this fight won't last long.

Tom Taylor: What an utterly pointless fight this is.

Gable Steveson is arguably the hottest prospect in all of MMA right now. Sean Sharaf is barely above the .500 mark, with stoppage losses in his first two UFC appearances. Whether Steveson chooses to lean on his wrestling or test out his developing striking, he is going to win this one quickly and decisively—and we will learn basically nothing new about him in the process.

Hopefully, the UFC takes off the training wheels for him very soon and matches him up with somebody who actually has the skills to test him. This kind of matchmaking accomplishes nothing.

articles.title: Los vecinos de Ceuta multiplican su interés por los talleres de defensa personal: "Intentamos que no se queden en blanco"
articles.standfirst: En el Club African Warriors hacen seminarios de 90 minutos todos los martes a las 20h
articles.summary: En el Club African Warriors hacen seminarios de 90 minutos todos los martes a las 20h
articles.body: La situación de inseguridad y tensión que se vive en Ceuta ha disparado el interés por las artes marciales mixtas en el último mes. Son muchos los vecinos que están acudiendo a diferentes centros a formarse en técnicas de pelea y también en talleres de defensa personal, cuya demanda se ha multiplicado. "La defensa personal es una cosa que yo quise implantar cuando abrí el club, pero no funcionó. Sin embargo, ahora es lo que más demanda tiene. Vienen mujeres que necesitan aprender a defenderse", explica José Anaya, maestro en Club African Warriors. La organizadora de estos grupos es Ana Villegas: "Los primeros días que lo ofrecimos fue brutal. Abríamos con 30 plazas y se llenaron 40, luego 50 y hasta 60, pero el profesor dijo que no podíamos coger más de 50 para que entrasen bien en los dos tatamis. Vista la demanda, empezamos a hacerlo todos los martes. La gente tiene miedo y cada vez me escriben más personas", relata. Aprender a pelear en poco tiempo es muy complicado, sobre todo cuando se trata de alumnos nuevos que no hacen deporte y que no tienen nociones en deportes de contacto. "Lo que se intenta es que no se queden en blanco, porque enseñar a pelear a una persona en un seminario es imposible. Eso requiere mucho tiempo. Para tener un conocimiento de un arte marcial necesitas uno o dos años como mínimo, pero al menos pueden tener tres nociones de cómo reaccionar si te pasa algo: hacer ruido, no enfrentarte a un tío a puñetazos porque lo único que vas a conseguir es lesionarte y que vaya la agresión a más, métodos de escape, hacerte notar... Determinadas nociones para no quedarte bloqueada y poder defenderte. Son clases de una hora y media que hacemos los martes a las 20h", detalla Anaya. Pese a que la mayoría de las alumnas son mujeres, no se trata de algo exclusivo de ellas. "Antiguamente estaba pensado sólo para mujeres, pero ahora hay muchos chicos que vienen. Necesitan sentirse seguros porque saben que les puede pasar a ellos. Pueden sufrir robos, por ejemplo, no solo nos van a agredir a nosotras", desvela Ana. Además, son cursos orientados a cualquier edad: "Viene gente de 12 o 13 años, pero también de 60 o más".

articles.title: Luke Rockhold sees Joe Pyfer as UFC title threat, not Bo Nickal
articles.summary: Luke Rockhold dismisses Bo Nickal’s UFC title hopes
articles.body:
CORAL GABLES, Fla.—Luke Rockhold knows what it takes to become UFC middleweight champion and he doesn't see Bo Nickal making it.

That's at least compared to Joe Pyfer, who wrestles Rockhold at RAF 13 this Friday at Watco Center. Pyfer is currently a top 10 contender in the UFC at 185 pounds, with Nickal—a three-division NCAA wrestling champion and one of the most highly touted prospects in recent memory—still working his way up the rankings.

Rockhold has previously been critical of Nickal's attitude , calling him "condescending," and he kept that same energy when asked to compare Nickal and Pyfer.

"Joe is relevant in my mind right now," Rockhold told MMA Fighting's Mike Heck. "He's a very tough dude. He's a threat for the title, which I don't see Bo at the moment at all."

Nickal won his first four UFC fights before being stopped by veteran Reinier de Ridder at UFC Des Moines. He has rebounded with back-to-back knockouts over Kyle Daukaus and Rodolfo Vieira, but still has some work to do compared to Pyfer. "Bodybagz" has won four straight fights and is coming off of a second-round TKO over two-time middleweight champion Israel Adesanya.

That's one reason why Rockhold sees Pyfer as his ideal opponent right now.

"This dude, he's a real threat, he's got a lot of momentum," Rockhold said. "A lot of hype. So it's motivating for me to put on my shoes, get back in the gym, get out of the bar scene, and go have some fun in the gym.

"Work like a kid, that's what it's all about, and go out there and perform and shut this kid down. I know he's a big tough guy, but I've been in the game a long time and I think I can beat him in a lot of ways."

To prepare for Pyfer, Rockhold has worked with fellow former middleweight champion Khamzat Chimaev, who also competes Friday at RAF 13. Chimaev wrestles Gilbert Burns in a rematch of sorts from their Fight of the Night-winning scrap at UFC 273, where Chimaev earned a hard-fought decision victory.

Rockhold considers Chimaev to have an elite work ethic.

"Khamzat, he's as tough as they come," Rockhold said. "That guy's always on. Doesn't take any days off. He's always putting in the work and he's as tough as a wrestler as you're going to get in MMA, so that's going to be a tough battle for Gilbert in this one."

articles.title: Luke Rockhold names 'only two people' he'd fight in MMA
articles.summary: Luke Rockhold isn't keen on signing with an MMA promotion, but two fighters would interest him in a return to the sport.
articles.body:
MIAMI – Luke Rockhold isn't keen on signing with an MMA promotion, but two fighters would interest him in a return to the sport.

Rockhold (16-6) hasn't competed in MMA since losing a blood-and-guts war to Paulo Costa at UFC 278 in August 2022, although he has remained active in Karate Combat, boxing, Bare Knuckle Boxing, and Real American Freestyle. The former UFC and Strikeforce middleweight champion was asked if he has any interest in joining forces with his old promoter, Scott Coker, who just launched Ki MMA.

"Nah," Rockhold told MMA Junkie. "I think a ring is cool. I think what he's doing, Scott has always been able to put together big stuff, so I think the ring is a very cool aspect of viewership. It's something sexy that the cage doesn't present, and that white ring is going to be very visible. You're going to be able to see a lot of knees and kicks, and sh*t flies very clearly and cleanly, and it's fun to watch. So, I hope the best for him."

Rockhold meets UFC middleweight contender Joe Pyfer in a light heavyweight wrestling match Friday at RAF 13. When asked if MMA is in his future, Rockhold said he'd entertain two fights only.

"There's only going to be a few fights I'd entertain in life – Mike Perry in MMA will be fun. I would love to whoop his little ass," Rockhold said. "Dillon Danis, I'd love to whoop his ass, too. That's probably the only two people I'd fight in MMA. I'd f*cking sh*t on their face (laughs). I love Mike, but watch your back, Mike. Watch your back."

articles.title: Alexander Volkanovski Reveals Why Joshua Van Can Beat Alexandre Pantoja at UFC 331
articles.summary: The reigning featherweight champion believes Joshua Van has worked on his grappling enough to retain his flyweight crown at UFC 331.
articles.body:
UFC 331 is just 48 hours away , with the flyweight title on the line in the main event. Joshua Van will face Alexandre Pantoja in a rematch following their bizarre first meeting at UFC 323 . It has been nine months since the two first met in December 2025, and their fight ended in one of the strangest ways possible.

Pantoja lost his long-held flyweight title just 26 seconds into the opening round after suffering a freak elbow injury following an awkward fall. Van was suddenly crowned champion, but an obvious question remained over his reign: could he prove that he truly belonged at the top?

Van answered that question at UFC 328 . The 24-year-old, now the second-youngest champion in UFC history, put together a standout performance against Tatsuro Taira, stopping the Japanese contender via fifth-round TKO. However, many fans still believe Pantoja will humble Van in the rematch, arguing that the Brazilian would have done so in December 2025 had he not suffered the injury.

Alexander Volkanovski, however, sees things differently. The reigning featherweight champion believes Van has what it takes to edge Pantoja in the rematch. His prediction comes after the two champions previously trained together.

In a video on his YouTube channel , Volk said, "I remember when we were in America, he [Van] wanted to grapple with everyone. He wanted to go there and get some grappling rounds; that was the whole point. He'd come and ask me questions."

Fans have been reluctant to give Van much of a chance on the ground because of Pantoja's elite grappling game. The Brazilian owns a 30-6 record with eight knockouts, 12 submissions and 10 decisions. His 12 submission wins account for 40% of his professional victories and highlight just how dangerous he can be once a fight hits the mat.

However, Volkanovski believes Van has likely been working on his grappling, especially given his natural desire to keep learning. He added, "That's what I like to see. Me knowing that, knowing that he's working on these things and already would have been working in these positions, but trying to understand the game and why we're doing this."

Van enters the rematch with 75% takedown defense and a 61% takedown accuracy of his own. He isn't afraid to grapple when necessary, but his priority is usually getting back to his feet rather than accepting extended periods on the ground.

That was evident in his last outing, when Taira took him down eight times from 21 attempts and controlled him for more than 10 minutes. Against Pantoja, however, Van will be facing arguably the most dangerous grappler he has encountered in UFC flyweight history.

The big question now is how much the champion has improved since that fight. If Van can neutralize Pantoja's grappling threat, he could have a much different night than many fans are expecting at UFC 331.

articles.title: John Hedges vs Pat Brown: Brown targets British title and famous nights
articles.summary: While British boxing fans' focus has been on world titles in recent weeks, with failed tilts by Conor Benn and Moses Itauma, Pat Brown has been preparing for a domestic bout where victory will enhance his own fast-growing reputation.
articles.body:
While British boxing fans' focus has been on world titles in recent weeks, with failed tilts by Conor Benn and Moses Itauma , Pat Brown has been preparing for a domestic bout where victory will enhance his own fast-growing reputation.

The Manchester-born cruiserweight headlines at the Co-op Live on Saturday with the coveted British and Commonwealth titles up for grabs, but he must come through the undefeated John Hedges.

As a Team GB Olympian, who featured at the 2024 Games in Paris , the hype around Brown, 26, is understandable but his main aim is delivering for his family.

When asked about the importance of being crowned British champion, Brown told BBC Sport: "It's a journey, I want to look back on my career and have the memories.

"It's a lovely belt and people say it's better than a world title because of the history and the way it looks.

"As long as I can put it on my dad's shoulders and show it to my family, then that's all I care about.

"I want to keep putting massive nights on for people and, whether that's boxing at world level or this level, it makes no odds to me."

Essex-born Hedges, who is unbeaten in 12 fights, represents the toughest test of Brown's short professional career to date.

But a relaxed Brown recalled the wise words of his biggest inspiration, his father, that there's "always someone harder around the corner".

"That's to keep me humble. You can't go thinking you're the bee's knees all the time," Brown added.

"I wouldn't be in this game if I didn't think I could fight anyone. I'll always get in the ring with anyone; that's the way my dad built me.

"Ever since I was a kid, whenever the phone went for a fight, he'd always say 'yes'. It doesn't matter about records or who they are, it's just boxing.

"If I feared someone in the sport, then it's not for me. I'll just walk away."

When Matchroom hastily arranged an event to officially announce Brown's signing in 2024 , around 300 fans turned out to catch a glimpse of the highly touted amateur.

But persuading 2,000 people to sit in a chilly Planet Ice in Altrincham on a Friday night may be an even better example of Brown's potential drawing power.

Saturday's fight was originally scheduled to take place there too but support from his fanbase meant a larger venue was required.

"Altrincham will always have a place in my heart, especially with people moaning how cold it is in there," Brown said.

"The only downfall are the changing rooms are quite small. I'm quite tall and the ceiling is a bit low, so it'll be nice to be in a big, open changing room.

"I used to go to that ice rink when I was a kid. To think I've actually headlined there on my debut – I can look and smile."

Brown, who has stopped all six of his opponents with four of his wins coming inside two rounds, has fast established himself as a prospect. He is also aware that, with Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury in the twilight of their careers, British boxing is craving its next star.

"It's nice, but I never look at it and crave it," he said.

"People will either like me or they won't. I'm never going to change, so if it comes and the country is getting behind me, that's brilliant."

Old Trafford fight 'would mean everything'

As Brown speaks to BBC Sport, the view of Old Trafford - the home of his beloved Manchester United - sits in the background.

Not since 1993 has the stadium hosted a boxing match, that being when Chris Eubank and Nigel Benn's unification bout ended in a draw.

But as Katie Taylor proved on 5 September, barriers are made to be broken after her spectacular Croke Park send-off.

When asked about the prospect of fighting at the Theatre of Dreams one day, Brown's face lights up.

"Ever since I was a kid, I've been there," Brown said.

"My house was only 15 minutes away from Old Trafford. When I watched on TV and United were playing at home, I used to feel warm inside watching it because I used to think 'that's my home'.

"If I could ever headline there, it would be a dream come true. That means more to me than belts.

"If I could headline at Old Trafford and walk out with all the people there loving it, that would mean everything."

Manchester is used to getting behind its own, most famously in boxing the iconic Ricky Hatton. Brown still has a long way to go, but Saturday presents his latest opportunity to make his own mark.

articles.summary: MMA News: Jon Anik believes Ilia Topuria’s comments about Justin Gaethje’s gloves could be part of a bigger plan to build interest in a rematch. The UFC comment.
articles.body: Jon Anik believes Ilia Topuria’s comments about Justin Gaethje’s gloves could be part of a bigger plan to build interest in a rematch. The UFC commentator has suggested that Topuria may be using the controversy to create a storyline around a second fight with Gaethje. The two fighters could meet again after their first bout at UFC Freedom 250.Anik also revealed that there are already “internal conversations” about a possible Gaethje vs. Topuria 2. While Topuria has expressed interest in returning to action, Gaethje has also made it clear that he would welcome another meeting. The developing storyline could give the UFC a major fight to consider for the lightweight division.Jon Anik explains why Ilia Topuria vs Justin Gaethje 2 could happenJustin Gaethje defeated Ilia Topuria by fourth-round TKO at the White House on June 14, 2026. The victory made Gaethje the undisputed UFC lightweight champion and handed Topuria the first defeat of his professional career.The fight has continued to generate attention because of Topuria’s later comments about Gaethje’s gloves. The former champion suggested that something unusual may have been involved.Topuria recently returned to social media after completing his medical tests. He wrote on X, “Final medical tests done. I’m back.”He later took another shot at Gaethje and referenced the glove controversy.“To all the clowns who’ve been talking s–t and counting me out this whole time, here I am. Now let’s see who’s got the balls. Thanks to everyone for the support. Next time I’ll make sure they check Justin’s gloves so he doesn’t put anything weird on them. See you soon,” he wrote on X.Gaethje responded to the accusation, “94 days and the best you could come up with is a lame excuse. As terrible as your last performance. Do better kid.”There have been no public findings from UFC officials showing that Gaethje’s gloves contained anything unusual. The claims remain unproven.Anik now believes the comments could serve another purpose. In his view, Topuria may be helping create a storyline that could make a rematch more attractive.The UFC commentator has also said that discussions about a second fight are already taking place within the promotion.A rematch is not the only possible option for Topuria. Anik previously mentioned Paddy Pimblett as another logical opponent for the former champion.However, Anik believes the UFC could prefer putting Topuria directly back into a title fight. The success of the first Gaethje-Topuria event could influence that decision.Anik has also discussed Gaethje’s priorities while assessing his future. He said, “I say that with all due respect. I think Justin is far more concerned with his show money than he is with who he’s actually fighting.”For now, Gaethje remains open to facing Topuria again and Topuria has also made it clear that he wants to return.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Van vs Pantoja 2, ¿la revancha más esperada de la UFC?
articles.standfirst: En su primer enfrentamiento el peelador birmano se aprovechó de una grave lesión del brasileño para arrebatarle el cinturón de peso mosca, y ahora toda la carne está en el asador
articles.summary: En su primer enfrentamiento el peelador birmano se aprovechó de una grave lesión del brasileño para arrebatarle el cinturón de peso mosca, y ahora toda la carne está en el asador
articles.body: Hace no tanto, era impensable que una pelea titular de peso mosca encabezase una cartelera numerada. Sin embargo, las 125 libras se han convertido en una de las categorías más mediáticas de la UFC, y este fin de semana en Los Ángeles el UFC 331 estará encabezado por una de las revanchas más esperadas de los últimos tiempos: Joshua Van (17-2) vs Alexandre Pantoja (30-6). El pasado diciembre, Pantoja se enfrentó al peleador birmano en su quinta defensa de cinturón, con el objetivo de seguir asentándose como el segundo mejor peleador de la historia de la división tras Demetrious Johnson. Sin embargo, nada más comenzar el combate Van bloqueó una patada del brasileño y éste se dislocó el codo al apoyar en el suelo. El combate se paró de inmediato y Joshua se coronó como nuevo campeón de peso mosca contra todo pronóstico. Mientras 'The Cannibal' se recuperaba de su grave lesión, Van continuó activo, y en mayo noqueó a Tatsuro Taira tras un gran combate para realizar su primera defensa. Sin embargo, esta revancha era un secreto a voces, y por fin se hará realidad. Ambos mantienen una rivalidad que se extiende a las ruedas de prensa, ya que Pantoja afirma que él sigue siendo el verdadero campeón mientras Joshua no para de mofarse de él ahora que tiene el cinturón en sus manos. A sus 36 años, hay mucha incertidumbre en torno a la figura del brasileño, ya que no es fácil volver de una lesión así después de tanto tiempo de inactividad. Es cierto que ha vencido a casi todos los grandes nombres de la división, que en el striking es bastante correcto y en el suelo es superior a Van, pero el birmano tiene 24 años y en cada pelea que realiza se ve mucho mejor que en la anterior. La evolución de 'Fearless' está siendo increíble, y está destinado a hacer historia al acumular 10 victorias en la UFC en apenas tres años. Para poner en perspectiva, Pantoja lleva 14 victorias en toda su carrera en la compañía y es considerado el segundo mejor de la división. "Ya te he ganado una vez, y voy a volver a hacerlo este sábado", le decía Van en la rueda de prensa oficial, mientras que Pantoja afirmaba que "en 20 segundos que duró la última pelea solo trato de abrazarme, quizás intente lo mismo esta vez y estoy preparado para ello". En cuanto a las faltas de respeto de Van hacia Pantoja, el brasileño tampoco se lo toma personal, ya que cuando se cierren las puertas del octágono podrán saldar sus cuentas. "No le entiendo, a veces dice que soy el mejor y otras que me va a ganar. En la primera pelea él en su mente de verdad piensa que me ganó, y este sábado tendrá la oportunidad de demostrarlo", sentenció.

articles.title: Craig Richards looks to relaunch world championship charge against Radivoje Kalajdzic on September 26 live on Sky Sports
articles.summary: Craig Richards fights Radivoje Kalajdzic in the chief support to Johnny Fisher vs Michael Pirotton on September 26, live on Sky Sports; victory can put Richards back into world title contention; "My story hasn't been written yet," Richards insists
articles.body:
Richards fights Belgrade's Radivoje Kalajdzic in the chief support to Johnny Fisher vs Michael Pirotton.

The man from Crystal Palace is determined to beat Kalajdzic to return to world championship class.

Kalajdzic is a top-quality operator who is coming off an excellent knockout win over former WBC world champion Oleksandr Gvozdyk. He has previously boxed Artur Beterbiev and knocked out former world title challenger Sullivan Barrera too.

"I think going out there and putting on a statement performance against him puts my name in a hat for that world title, 100 per cent," Richards told Sky Sports . "I'm locked in. I'm ready to do a job.

In 2021, Richards challenged Dmitry Bivol for the WBA light-heavyweight title, losing on a unanimous but closer than expected decision. Bivol subsequently established himself as the best in the division when he beat Beterbiev.

That is the level Richards wants to get back to.

"My story hasn't been written yet," the Londoner declared. "I didn't do all of this and sacrifice everything to not accomplish my goals to be a world champion.

"So I feel like I should get a reward. I'm not being entitled, but I feel like the work I put in, I should get something back out of it. And that's to be world champion.

"For sure, co-main-event fight in front of a home crowd, you know it's a good place to start.

"Execute on the night and we move forward from there."

Watch Craig Richards vs Radivoje Kalajdzic live on Sky Sports on September 26.

articles.title: Eddie Hearn Raises Major Doubt About Conor Benn's Future After Ryan Garcia Loss
articles.summary: Eddie Hearn says Conor Benn will be done within a year and may not fight again after Ryan Garcia stopped him in two rounds. His full reaction.
articles.body:
Conor Benn was on the wrong end of a vicious TKO loss to Ryan Garcia on Saturday and now there are questions as to whether he'll fight again. It's important to mention that some of these questions are coming from Benn's former promoter Eddie Hearn. Benn left Hearn to sign with rival Dana White's Zuffa Boxing. Garcia blew Benn away after the latter had to endure a brutal weight cut to get down to 147 pounds. Benn was paid handsomely for his sacrifice, but he did take the kind of loss that changes a fighter. What's next for Benn? Let's talk boxing.

Ryan Garcia def. Conor Benn, TKO, Round 2

Second career loss, first world title attempt

Promoted Benn at Matchroom until Benn signed with Zuffa Boxing in February

Unsure of his next move, priority is family

Hearn's verdict came on iFL TV, and he opened with an admission : he did not watch the fight. He watched Misfits Boxing and went to bed. On Benn's future, Hearn said he will be done within a year, may have one more fight and may not fight again at all, because he has made his money.

He also said Benn looked lost and like a rabbit in headlights, and that Saturday answered the world-class question in the negative. Hearn still sees money in a Chris Eubank Jr. trilogy.

Benn admitted on Instagram that he doesn't know what's next for him.

Benn did put himself through a brutal weight cut, but I also think he hit his talent/performance ceiling. Benn is as tough as they come and he is a solid puncher. That said, he has always had footwork and defensive issues. Both of those things reared their ugly heads on Saturday. Benn was so preoccupied with Garcia's vaunted left hook that he overcompensated and forgot about the right hand.

That was the punch that put him down and effectively ended his night. Did it end his career? Maybe. Benn made enough money over the past two fights that he could probably walk off into the sunset and be fine for the rest of his life. However, he is a competitor and it might be too tough for him to stay away from the glory that a fighter can only find in the ring. We'll see, but Hearn probably isn't way off base.
